description: Golden retrieval set. Labels map to chunks via 'relevant_snippets' (case-insensitive substring match after whitespace normalization) so labels survive re-indexing. A retrieval hits when any returned chunk contains a snippet.

questions.question: What is a large language model?
relevant_snippets: A large language model (LLM) is a computational model trained on a vast amount of data
questions.reference_answer: A computational model trained on vast amounts of data for natural language processing tasks, especially language generation; the largest are GPTs underlying modern chatbots.

questions.question: What architecture do modern LLMs use and when was it introduced?
relevant_snippets: transformer architecture, introduced in 2017, replaced recurrence with self-attention
questions.reference_answer: The transformer architecture, introduced in 2017, which replaced recurrence with self-attention.

questions.question: How does RLHF improve LLM behavior?
relevant_snippets: training a reward model to predict which text humans prefer
questions.reference_answer: It trains a reward model to predict human preferences, then fine-tunes the LLM via reinforcement learning to satisfy that reward, favoring truthful, helpful, harmless answers.

questions.question: Which GPT model first caught widespread public attention and why?
relevant_snippets: GPT-2 in 2019 that caught widespread attention
questions.reference_answer: GPT-2 in 2019, because OpenAI initially deemed it too powerful to release publicly over malicious-use fears.

questions.question: Which open-weight model released in January 2025 performs comparably to OpenAI o1?
relevant_snippets: DeepSeek R1
671-billion-parameter open-weight model
questions.reference_answer: DeepSeek R1, a 671-billion-parameter open-weight model released January 2025.

questions.question: What is byte-pair encoding used for in LLM training?
relevant_snippets: byte-pair encoding (BPE)
questions.reference_answer: A tokenization algorithm: starting from characters, it iteratively merges the most frequent adjacent pairs into longer n-grams to build a vocabulary for converting text to tokens.

questions.question: What did it cost to train GPT-2 versus PaLM?
questions.reference_answer: GPT-2 cost about $50,000 in 2019; PaLM cost about $8 million in 2022.

questions.question: What context window size can Google Gemini 1.5 handle?
relevant_snippets: context window of up to 1 million tokens
questions.reference_answer: Up to 1 million tokens.

questions.question: What is the difference between autoregressive and masked pre-training?
relevant_snippets: autoregressive (i.e. predicting how the segment continues
questions.reference_answer: Autoregressive models predict how a segment continues (GPT); masked models fill in missing parts of a segment (BERT).

questions.question: What are emergent abilities in LLMs?
relevant_snippets: larger models acquire
questions.reference_answer: Abilities that appear abruptly at scale via breaks in scaling-law curves, arising from complex component interactions rather than explicit programming.

questions.question: Define perplexity for a language model.
relevant_snippets: perplexity is the exponential of the average negative log likelihood per token
questions.reference_answer: The exponential of average negative log likelihood per token; lower perplexity means better prediction of the corpus.

questions.question: How does chain-of-thought prompting work?
relevant_snippets: break the question down autonomously
questions.reference_answer: The LLM is shown examples that verbally break down the thought process before answering, then mimics them, generating intermediate steps that improve correctness on complex questions.

questions.question: What is mechanistic interpretability?
relevant_snippets: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to precisely identify
questions.reference_answer: Research that reverse-engineers how individual neurons or circuits in LLMs produce behaviors, aiming to detect safety concerns like bias or deception before deployment.

questions.question: Why do LLM hallucinations occur?
relevant_snippets: memorization of training data combined with extrapolation beyond factual boundaries
questions.reference_answer: They arise partly from memorizing training data combined with extrapolation beyond factual boundaries.

questions.question: What is prompt injection?
relevant_snippets: messages that appear to come from the assistant or the developer
questions.reference_answer: Crafting user messages that appear to come from the assistant or developer, potentially overcoming safeguards (jailbreaking).

questions.question: What is retrieval-augmented generation?
relevant_snippets: technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information
questions.reference_answer: A technique enabling LLMs to retrieve and incorporate information from external sources before responding, supplementing training data with domain-specific or updated knowledge.

questions.question: When was the term RAG first introduced?
relevant_snippets: first introduced in a 2020 research paper
questions.reference_answer: In a 2020 research paper.

questions.question: What is prompt stuffing in RAG?
relevant_snippets: has been called "prompt stuffing"
questions.reference_answer: Adding retrieved context to the user input early in the prompt so the LLM prioritizes supplied data over its training knowledge.

questions.question: Name three chunking strategies for RAG.
relevant_snippets: Fixed length with overlap
Syntax-based chunks
File format-based chunking
questions.reference_answer: Fixed-length with overlap, syntax-based chunking (e.g., sentences via spaCy/NLTK), and file-format-based chunking respecting natural structures like functions or HTML elements.

questions.question: What is hybrid search in the context of RAG?
relevant_snippets: traditional text search, add those results
questions.reference_answer: Combining vector search results with traditional text search results and feeding both into the LLM, mitigating cases where vector search misses key facts.

questions.question: Does RAG eliminate hallucinations?
relevant_snippets: does not prevent hallucinations
questions.reference_answer: No — the LLM can still hallucinate around the source material in its response.

questions.question: What is the Inverse Cloze Task?
relevant_snippets: Inverse Cloze Task (ICT), a technique that helps the model learn retrieval patterns by predicting masked text within documents
questions.reference_answer: A pre-training technique for retrievers where the model learns retrieval patterns by predicting masked text within documents.

questions.question: What is RAG poisoning?
relevant_snippets: retrieve factually correct but misleading sources
questions.reference_answer: When RAG systems retrieve factually correct but misleading sources, misinterpret context, or merge conflicting sources into misleading responses.

questions.question: How did the James Webb Space Telescope error affect Google?
relevant_snippets: incorrect information about the James Webb Space Telescope
questions.reference_answer: Google Bard gave incorrect JWST information at its demo, contributing to a $100 billion decline in Alphabet's stock value.

questions.question: Who created LangChain and when?
relevant_snippets: launched in October 2022 as an open source project by Harrison Chase
questions.reference_answer: Harrison Chase launched it as an open-source project in October 2022.

questions.question: What is LangServe?
relevant_snippets: deployment tool to host LCEL code as a production-ready API
questions.reference_answer: A deployment tool (October 2023) that hosts LCEL code as a production-ready API.

questions.question: What is LCEL?
relevant_snippets: provides a declarative way to define chains of actions
questions.reference_answer: The LangChain Expression Language, introduced Q3 2023 — a declarative way to define chains of actions.

questions.question: What is LangSmith?
relevant_snippets: observability and evaluation platform for LLM applications
questions.reference_answer: A closed-source observability and evaluation platform for LLM applications, released February 2024.

questions.question: Which Chinese company released an open-weight reasoning model rivaling OpenAI o1, and how many parameters does it have?
relevant_snippets: DeepSeek-R1
comparable performance to OpenAI's o1
questions.reference_answer: DeepSeek released DeepSeek-R1, a 671-billion-parameter open-weight reasoning model comparable to o1 and cheaper to operate.

questions.question: Which venture firms invested in LangChain?
relevant_snippets: Sequoia Capital
questions.reference_answer: Sequoia Capital led the Series A (over $20M at a $200M+ valuation), a week after Benchmark's $10M seed.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
How do I bake sourdough bread at home?
What is the current price of Bitcoin?
Who proposed the transformer architecture and in which paper?
relevant_snippets: the transformer architecture was proposed in the 2017 paper
Attention Is All You Need
questions.reference_answer: Researchers at Google, in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need".

questions.question: What architecture dominated long sequence modelling before transformers?
relevant_snippets: architecture for long sequence modelling until the 2017 publication of transformers
questions.reference_answer: LSTM (recurrent) architectures dominated until transformers were published in 2017.

questions.question: What is a vector database?
relevant_snippets: database that stores and retrieves embeddings of data in vector space
questions.reference_answer: A database (also called vector store or vector search engine) that stores and retrieves embeddings of data in vector space, enabling efficient similarity search.

questions.question: Which toolkit popularized training word embeddings?
relevant_snippets: word2vec, a word embedding toolkit that can train vector space model
questions.reference_answer: word2vec, a toolkit for training vector space models of words.

questions.question: Whose probabilistic framework underlies the BM25 ranking function?
relevant_snippets: Robertson
Spärck
questions.reference_answer: The probabilistic retrieval framework developed by Stephen Robertson and Karen Spärck Jones.

questions.question: What is a knowledge graph?
relevant_snippets: knowledge base that uses a graph-structured data model or topology to represent
questions.reference_answer: A knowledge base that uses a graph-structured data model to integrate data, representing entities and their relationships.

questions.question: Which prompting technique helps LLMs handle multi-step reasoning?
relevant_snippets: chain-of-thought techniques were developed to help llms handle multi-step re
questions.reference_answer: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting, developed to help LLMs handle multi-step reasoning.

questions.question: Which tokenization algorithms are used when preparing text for large language models?
relevant_snippets: byte-pair encoding (bpe) and wordpiece
byte pair encoding (bpe) and the unigram language model
questions.reference_answer: LLMs preprocess text with subword tokenization: byte-pair encoding plus WordPiece; the transformer article additionally pairs BPE with the unigram language model.

questions.question: In retrieval-augmented generation, where are the document embeddings stored?
relevant_snippets: these embeddings are then stored in a vector database
stores and retrieves embeddings of data in vector space
questions.reference_answer: RAG stores converted embeddings in a vector database — a system that stores and retrieves embeddings in vector space for similarity-based retrieval.

questions.question: RAG can operate on which structured data representation, and how is that structure defined?
relevant_snippets: for example knowledge graphs
graph-structured data model or topology to represent
questions.reference_answer: RAG accepts structured data such as knowledge graphs; a knowledge graph uses a graph-structured data model/topology to represent entities and relationships.

questions.question: Chain-of-thought prompting targets multi-step reasoning in models built on which architecture?
relevant_snippets: chain-of-thought techniques were developed to help llms handle multi-step re
transformer architecture, introduced in 2017
questions.reference_answer: CoT prompting helps LLMs reason step-by-step; those LLMs are built on the transformer architecture introduced in 2017.

questions.question: The architecture behind today's language models was proposed where, and what preceded it for long sequences?
relevant_snippets: proposed in the 2017 paper
long sequence modelling until the 2017 publication
questions.reference_answer: The transformer was proposed in the 2017 paper "Attention Is All You Need"; before it, LSTM-style recurrent architectures handled long sequence modelling.

questions.question: What kind of mathematical objects does a vector search engine store, and which toolkit first made training them for words popular?
relevant_snippets: embeddings of data in vector space
word2vec, a word embedding toolkit
questions.reference_answer: Vector databases store and retrieve embeddings (dense vectors); word2vec popularized training such vectors for words.
